Research Spotlight

AI (Mis)attribution

Do people judge the same interaction differently when they believe artificial intelligence is involved?

In an online study, participants rated a conversation as more natural when they believed both speakers were human—even though every condition used the same transcript.

Behavior Analysis

Data reveals patterns.Care gives them purpose.

I am drawn to behavior analysis because it brings care and evidence into the same room. Studying patterns over time can help teams understand what is working, what needs to change, and how support can better reflect the person receiving it.

Data does not replace the human story. It can help us listen more carefully, contribute to individualized decisions, and keep independence, dignity, and informed choice in view.

  1. Observe
  2. Measure
  3. Understand
  4. Adjust
  5. Review

Patterns become useful when they lead to thoughtful action.

ABA-Informed Design Pathway

A clearer path from observation to useful change.

Behavioral ideas are translated into everyday design decisions. Technical terms appear only where they add precision.

  1. 01

    Attending

    Attention and Relevance

    People notice what feels clear, relevant, and connected to their immediate needs. Strong hierarchy helps important information become easier to find without demanding attention through noise.

    Design implication: make the essential path visible before adding detail.
  2. 02

    Discriminative cues

    Clear Cues and Orientation

    A person should be able to understand where they are, what is available, and what will happen next. Familiar cues and predictable structure reduce uncertainty.

    Design implication: use stable labels, states, and navigation patterns.
  3. 03

    Prompting and fading

    Learning in Manageable Steps

    Complex information becomes easier to understand when it is introduced gradually and supported by clear examples, feedback, and opportunities to succeed.

    Design implication: disclose complexity as it becomes useful.
  4. 04

    Feedback

    Feedback, Trust, and Continuity

    Reliable feedback helps people understand the result of an action. Consistency over time builds confidence and makes an experience feel dependable.

    Design implication: show what happened and preserve context.
  5. 05

    Socially meaningful outcomes

    Measure, Learn, and Refine

    A useful system should be evaluated by what people can accomplish with it. Observe outcomes, identify barriers, and improve the environment when the data shows that change is needed.

    Design implication: measure success against meaningful tasks.

The pathway is grounded in behavior-analysis literature on attending, stimulus control, prompting, fading, feedback, and socially meaningful outcomes. It also reflects professional ethics emphasizing dignity, compassion, self-determination, and informed choice. Read the full approach and sources.
